newsitem.title: USA: U.S. admiral says forces fire 27 missiles at Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. admiral says forces fire 27 missiles at Iraq.

text.p: U.S. forces fired a total of 27 sea-launched and air-launched cruise missiles on Tuesday at targets in southern Iraq, an American admiral said.

"At 7.15 this morning (0415 GMT) U.S. naval and air forces executed air strikes against Iraqi military sites," Rear Admiral Edward Moore, commander of American naval forces in the Gulf, told reporters aboard the aircraft carrier Carl Vinson.

"The strikes were conducted with both shipboard-launched Tomahawk cruise missiles and conventional air launched cruise missiles and were directed against Iraqi air defence sites and command and control facilities," Moore said.
"The strikes were ordered as a warning to Iraq to adhere to requirements outlined in United Nations resolutions."

He added the targets were in the southern Iraq. He said 13 missiles were fired from B-52 bombers and 14 missiles were fired from the USS Laboon guided missile destroyer and the USS Shilo cruiser in the Gulf.
In Washington, defence officials said the U.S. raids were launched on orders from President Bill Clinton in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.
